q1_issues.issue: The "to win the nomination" consequence is folded into the SAME strength-0.0 conjunction as the receiving event, so the rule denies only the conjunction (received-enough-votes AND can-win) instead of denying that anyone received enough votes — a strictly weaker claim, satisfiable by someone who did receive enough votes but cannot win; the "enough … to V" pattern keeps the consequence as its own statement beside the Degree atom.

q2_gaps: negation scoping over an "enough N to V" degree-consequence construction — the instruction set fixes the positive shape (Degree … quantity sufficient plus the positive action) but not how the consequence is carried, or whether it flips, when the matrix clause is denied
notes: The negative-universal rule form over (Member $x person) at strength 0.0, the per-binding Skolem vote group with GroupOf, the projected typing of the definite nomination and the QuantifierPhrase companion all follow the instruction set.
